comment: Hand-entered inputs of features-centre.json (Galactic centre within about 300 pc of Sgr A*). Every value carries evidence { source, quote } checked against the fetched paper by centre.mjs. Positions: SIMBAD or Kauffmann et al. 2017 Table 1, at the distance of Sgr A* (GRAVITY Collaboration 2019).

features.description: The densest star cluster in the Galaxy, centred on the supermassive black hole Sgr A*: tens of millions of mostly old stars within a few parsecs, plus a young population near the black hole. It is flattened along the Galactic plane and rotates in the same sense as the Galaxy. Its density falls roughly as r^-2 within a few parsecs and as steeply as r^-3 around 5 pc (Schödel et al. 2014). Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016 quote a lower mass of 1.8e7 Msun with the same half-light radius and axis ratio. Placed at Sgr A*; r is the half-light radius.

features.description: A flattened, dense, rotating disc of stars that dominates the gravity between about 30 and 300 pc from the centre, sharing its volume with the Central Molecular Zone. Dynamical model of Sormani et al. 2022; the older photometric decomposition of Launhardt et al. 2002 gives a larger outer radius (230 pc) and scale height (45 pc), and a mass of 1.4e9 Msun for the whole nuclear bulge. Placed at Sgr A*; r is the Launhardt et al. radius.

features.description: The ring of dense, warm and turbulent molecular gas in the inner few hundred parsecs, fed by gas flowing in along the bar's dust lanes. It holds the major Galactic-centre clouds (Sgr B2, the dust ridge with the Brick, the 20 and 50 km/s clouds, Sgr C) yet forms stars at only about 0.07 Msun per year. It is lopsided: roughly three-quarters of the emission is at positive longitudes. Placed at Sgr A*; r is the upper end of the published ring radius.

features.description: One of the densest young star clusters in the Galaxy, a few million years old, in the Central Molecular Zone near the Radio Arc. Its initial mass function is top-heavy (relatively more massive stars than in the solar neighbourhood). Its distance along the line of sight is not measured, so it is placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position).

features.description: A massive young cluster rich in evolved massive stars (Wolf-Rayet stars, luminous blue variables such as the Pistol Star, and red supergiants), named after five bright infrared members. The age comes from matching its Wolf-Rayet population to models of a 60 Msun star, because the extinction law is too uncertain for isochrone fitting (Clark et al. 2018). Its distance along the line of sight is not measured, so it is placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position).

features.description: The most massive molecular cloud complex in the Galaxy and the site of most of the present-day star formation in the Central Molecular Zone, with the protoclusters Sgr B2(N) and Sgr B2(M). Radius and mass of Kauffmann et al. 2017 refer to the area above an H2 column density of 9e22 cm^-2. Maser parallaxes put it about 130 +- 60 pc from Sgr A*, in front of it; the label uses the SIMBAD direction at the distance of Sgr A*.

features.description: A massive, cold, dense cloud that is dark even in the mid-infrared against the bright Galactic-centre background, hence the nickname. It is almost devoid of star formation despite its mass and density, making it a test case for how star formation is suppressed in the Central Molecular Zone. First cloud of the 'dust ridge' towards Sgr B2. Placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position).

features.description: Star-forming complex at the negative-longitude end of the Central Molecular Zone, on the opposite side from Sgr B2, with an HII region powered by at least one O star and a cloud forming groups of hundreds of stars. Placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position).

features.description: One of the two 'Sgr A clouds', about 10 pc from Sgr A* in projection, named after its line-of-sight velocity. It forms groups of hundreds of stars, unlike its neighbour the 50 km/s cloud. The orbital model of Kruijssen et al. 2015 puts it at least 60 pc in front of Sgr A*; the label uses the (l, b) of Kauffmann et al. 2017 at the distance of Sgr A*.

features.description: The second 'Sgr A cloud', next to the supernova remnant Sgr A East, with which it is thought to interact. It is not forming stars as richly as the 20 km/s cloud although it has a similar mass and density. The orbital model of Kruijssen et al. 2015 puts it at least 60 pc in front of Sgr A*; the label uses the (l, b) of Kauffmann et al. 2017 at the distance of Sgr A*.

features.description: A supernova remnant only a few parsecs from Sgr A*: a non-thermal radio shell filled with hot, metal-rich X-ray gas (a 'mixed-morphology' remnant). It envelops Sgr A* and the circumnuclear disc in projection. Placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position).

features.description: A clumpy ring of warm, dense molecular gas and dust orbiting the supermassive black hole, the closest large gas reservoir to Sgr A*. Inside it lies the ionised minispiral (Sgr A West). Placed at the distance of Sgr A* (SIMBAD position); r = 5 pc is the middle of the published 3-7 pc outer radius.
